question.text: Under SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/OIAE/OIAE_IAD-1/P/CIR/2023/131 dated July 31, 2023, AIFs are required to:

answer.text: Maintain a physical ombudsman office in every SEBI regional center
Refuse all disputes that cannot be resolved within 7 days

Enrol on the MII-established ODR (Online Dispute Resolution) Portal, display a link to the ODR Portal on the home page of their websites and mobile apps, and ensure implementation of related processes
Charge a dispute-resolution fee from the complainant

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 11.7.8, AIFs must enrol on the ODR Portal set up by Market Infrastructure Institutions, display a link on their website/app home page, execute electronic agreements with MIIs and ODR Institutions, and train staff to handle SCORES and ODR references plus online conciliation and arbitration. **The Trap:** Physical regional ombudsman is not required. Refusing beyond 7 days violates the 21-day SCORES rule. Charging complainants violates SEBI's grievance-access principle. **Cross-Exam Context:** Grievance architecture tested in III-A (Compliance) and across SEBI intermediary exams. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Integrate SCORES, ODR, and internal grievance systems into a single ticketing platform. Disparate inbox/phone/portal tracking is how deadlines are missed — a unified dashboard is the single best investor-grievance control.
